If a learner counted only the interval from 70°F to 41°F, draw a line from 8:00 to 2:20 and label both endpoints. Practice with a final reading at 1:55 p.m.: the total becomes 5 hours 55 minutes, within the stated six-hour boundary if the other conditions are met.

theory.heading: Convert the review into action
theory.text: Choose one or two recurring or important topics based on actual reviewed evidence and the applicable exam outline, not on an assumed weakness. For each, specify a source, an action and a transfer check: for example, read the cooling provision, write a new timeline and explain both limits. If a question was slow but correct, test a similar case with different values; if it was wrong because the key was disputed, resolve the source issue before using it as evidence of performance. Leave unfinished reviews visible and avoid comparing raw percentages from different sets as if they shared a calibrated scale.

worked_case.scenario: An illustrative learner answers an AP/EP question incorrectly, chooses a cooling answer without checking the start time, and flags a clinical item with a questionable explanation. The learner's actual responses, if any, may differ.
worked_case.reasoning: For the purchase item, required EP is 24 lb at 80% yield, so total AP is 24 ÷ 0.80 = 30 lb. If 6 lb AP is available and bags hold 8 lb, the 24 lb shortfall requires three whole bags. For cooling, mark when 135°F, 70°F and 41°F were reached; assess both the first-stage and total intervals. For the disputed clinical item, review the exact claim and primary source before assigning a definite score. An item can be slow, guessed or disputed for different reasons. Variation: if the stock is 4 lb, the shortfall is 26 lb and four 8 lb bags are needed. This example does not describe the user's history.

questions.stem: A learner needs 25.6 lb EP at 80% yield, has 5 lb usable, uncommitted AP stock, and can buy only 8 lb bags. What is the minimum number of bags?
option_rationales: Two bags provide 16 lb against a 27 lb shortfall.
Three bags provide 24 lb, still short.
Correct: total AP is 32 lb; after 5 lb stock, 27 lb remains, so four bags supply 32 lb.
Five bags suffice but are not the minimum.

questions.stem: A cooling record reaches 70°F 90 minutes after 135°F and 41°F 6 hours 20 minutes after 135°F. Under the FDA 2026 model, what should the reviewer identify?
options: The first stage is late but the total is timely
The first stage is timely but the total is late
Both intervals meet the stated limits
A specific pathogen is proven present
option_rationales: The 90-minute first stage is within two hours.
Correct: the first stage is timely, but the total exceeds six hours.
The total is 20 minutes beyond the stated boundary.
A timing deviation alone does not identify a specific organism.

questions.stem: An answer explanation conflicts with its cited primary source. What should be done before using the item to assess performance?
options: Flag the conflict and verify the precise claim
Assume the answer key is always right
Invent a source that agrees with the key
Count the item as proof of a learner's weakness
option_rationales: Correct: a conflict needs resolution before confident scoring.
A key can contain an error or rely on an unstated condition.
Inventing evidence does not resolve the issue.
An unresolved item does not establish the cause of a response.

questions.stem: A learner answers correctly but had guessed between two options. What review best tests understanding?
options: Explain why one option fits and apply the rule to a changed case
Assume the whole domain is mastered
Memorize the position of the correct answer
Ignore the item because it was counted correct
option_rationales: Correct: explanation and a new case probe the reasoning behind the choice.
One guessed answer does not establish mastery.
Position memorization does not test the underlying concept.
A guess can reveal a useful uncertainty even when the answer is correct.

questions.stem: A patient has a low albumin value during an inflammatory illness. What is the safest review of a claim that albumin alone proves malnutrition?
options: Seek intake, weight and other relevant assessment findings
Use albumin alone to establish the diagnosis
Conclude the patient has normal nutrition status
Disregard all other clinical data
option_rationales: Correct: assessment uses multiple findings and context.
Albumin is affected by inflammation and is not alone an accepted diagnostic measure.
A low albumin value does not establish normal status either.
Relevant assessment data remain important.

review: If Day 39 was completed, choose one actual guessed or slow response and write a new value or changed condition; otherwise work the illustrative case.
Check a source conflict against the relevant edition and setting before counting it as certain.
Write one follow-up action with a specific source and an observable check; do not infer a persistent pattern from one item.

days.title: Final Check for Recurring Errors
objectives: Test whether a reasoning pattern actually repeats across new reviewed examples.
Apply clinical, quantitative, communication and safety principles to changed scenarios.
Identify unresolved sources and remaining coverage without relying on answer-letter recognition.

theory.heading: Suggested 90-minute sequence
theory.text: Spend 10 minutes selecting a pattern from your actual notes, if one is present; 25 minutes studying the transfer examples below; 20 minutes working the case and its variations; 20 minutes answering and reviewing the five authored questions; and 15 minutes recording follow-up and source checks. If you do not yet have repeated evidence, use the examples as practice and record the question as pending. No weakness is assumed.

theory.heading: What counts as a recurring pattern?
theory.text: A pattern is a provisional observation across multiple appropriate, reviewed examples, not one incorrect choice or several repetitions of the same memorized item. Identify the actual underlying action: using the wrong denominator, overlooking a time origin, choosing an intervention before assessing its cause, or assuming a source applies to another population. Check whether the pattern appears in new contexts and whether a clear explanation changes the result. Topic, difficulty, feedback and fatigue may vary. A learner may know a concept yet misread a qualifier in one case; avoid converting limited evidence into a fixed label.

theory.heading: Transfer a yield method
theory.text: A reliable formula is EP = AP × yield, where the yield applies to the specified product and final form. For 16 lb EP at 80% yield, calculate 16 ÷ 0.80 = 20 lb AP. For a second item, 18 lb AP at 80% yield provides 18 × 0.80 = 14.4 lb EP. The requested unknown changes the operation. Add stock and whole-package rounding only if the case supplies those facts and asks for an order. To check whether the concept transfers, write the units at each step and verify with the inverse relation, then change one fact such as the required form or yield.

theory.heading: Transfer an assessment decision
theory.text: A patient whose scale weight is stable but has new edema and reports reduced intake requires more context, not an invented exact tissue loss. Gather and verify weight history, intake, clinical condition and other relevant findings. A positive screen identifies possible nutrition risk and supports comprehensive assessment; it does not by itself determine a diagnosis or severity. Albumin and prealbumin can change with inflammation and are not stand-alone malnutrition diagnostic measures. A later intervention should address the assessed cause, and monitoring should measure the intended outcome. A change in scenario—from edema absent to edema present—changes the certainty of weight interpretation, not necessarily the diagnosis.

theory.heading: Transfer a time and temperature rule
theory.text: Under FDA Food Code 2026 §3-501.14 for cooked TCS food, compare both the interval from 135°F to 70°F and the total interval from 135°F to 41°F or lower. A batch reaching 70°F after 1 hour 20 minutes and 41°F after 5 hours 40 minutes meets those specified time limits, assuming reliable readings and applicable conditions. If the first-stage reading is instead after 2 hours 10 minutes, that first-stage limit is missed even when the final reading is within six hours. Record the two intervals separately. The Food Code is a model and local requirements should be checked for actual operations.

theory.heading: Transfer communication and quality concepts
theory.text: A person repeats a meal instruction incorrectly after the first explanation. Teach-back asks the practitioner to explain in a different way and request the person's description in their own words; it is a check of communication, not a test to label the person noncompliant. In a quality-improvement case, a small PDSA test compares an observed result with a prediction and informs the next cycle. An improvement in a single observation does not by itself prove causality or future performance. For each case, identify the objective, the evidence that would measure it and the next action rather than selecting an attractive but unrelated activity.

theory.heading: Resolve ambiguities and plan spaced review
theory.text: If an item omits a critical condition or its explanation conflicts with a cited source, record the issue and verify the exact claim before using the item as a performance measure. Check that the source edition, patient or production setting and units match the question. Use a new variation to test an intended principle without inventing a missing value. Document a next review date or session and one observable check, such as explaining both cooling limits or solving a new AP calculation. Five authored questions cannot establish readiness, and a short practice percentage is not the official CDR score.

worked_case.scenario: A service needs 25.2 lb usable vegetables at a verified 70% yield. It has 4 lb AP of uncommitted stock and buys whole 10 lb bags. A second scenario involves a patient with new edema and low intake; a third log shows cooling from 135°F to 70°F in 2 hours 10 minutes and to 41°F in 5 hours total.
worked_case.reasoning: Total AP required is 25.2 ÷ 0.70 = 36 lb; after 4 lb stock the shortfall is 32 lb, requiring four 10 lb bags. For the patient, gather and verify intake, weight history and relevant clinical findings; do not infer exact tissue loss from edema. The cooling first stage missed the two-hour limit under the named FDA 2026 model even though the final total was under six hours. Follow the relevant plan and jurisdiction for corrective action. Variation: if stock is 7 lb AP, the shortfall is 29 lb and three bags suffice. Explain the operation and unit at every step.

questions.stem: A service needs 23.4 lb EP at 90% yield, has 3 lb usable, uncommitted AP stock and buys 7 lb bags. What is the minimum order?
options: 2 bags
3 bags
4 bags
5 bags
option_rationales: Two bags supply only 14 lb against the 23 lb shortfall.
Three bags supply 21 lb, still short.
Correct: 23.4 ÷ 0.90 = 26 lb AP; after stock, 23 lb requires four bags.
Five bags meet the quantity but are not the minimum order.

questions.stem: A patient has stable measured weight, new edema and reduced reported intake. What is the best interpretation?
options: Fluid may obscure change; gather additional assessment data
Stable weight excludes loss of tissue
Edema proves exactly 5 kg of tissue loss
The intake report is irrelevant
option_rationales: Correct: edema can complicate weight interpretation and warrants contextual assessment.
Scale weight alone may mask underlying changes.
The exact amount of tissue loss cannot be calculated from the stated facts.
Reduced intake is relevant information to assess.

questions.stem: Under the stated FDA 2026 model, food takes 2 hours 10 minutes to cool from 135°F to 70°F, then reaches 41°F at 5 hours total. Which limit was missed?
options: The two-hour first stage
The six-hour total
Neither stated limit
Both limits
option_rationales: Correct: the first stage exceeds two hours.
The five-hour total is within six hours.
The first stage is late.
The total time is within the six-hour limit, so both were not missed.

questions.stem: A person cannot restate a care plan after the first explanation. Which teach-back response is best?
options: Explain again using a different approach and check in the person's own words
Label the person noncompliant
Ask only whether the person understood
Use more jargon to test vocabulary
option_rationales: Correct: revise the explanation and check communication again.
Difficulty restating a plan alone does not prove noncompliance.
A yes/no response alone does not show what was understood.
More jargon does not support clear communication.

questions.stem: A learner has answered one question incorrectly on a new topic. What is a defensible conclusion?
options: The single result identifies every persistent weakness
The response is one observation; test reasoning on more reviewed variations
The entire subject is mastered
The official score is determined
option_rationales: One observation is insufficient to establish every persistent pattern.
Correct: more reviewed cases can help test a tentative explanation.
One incorrect response does not establish mastery either.
A small practice result does not determine an official score.

review: Use actual notes, if available, to select one repeated pattern; otherwise record that the pattern is not yet established.
Create a variant of one calculation, one safety timeline or one assessment case and explain the answer without relying on its letter.
List any source or condition that remains unresolved and the next source to consult.

days.title: Light Review and Decision
objectives: Summarize actual coverage and available practice evidence without assuming a scheduled exam.
Apply a few changed-fact cases and identify unresolved questions.
Choose a cautious next study action without treating the review as an official score or guarantee.

theory.heading: Suggested 45-minute sequence
theory.text: Spend 8 minutes checking what has and has not been studied; 12 minutes on the worked case and variation; 15 minutes answering and reviewing the four questions; and 10 minutes deciding the next manageable action. If an earlier practice session was not completed or is stored on another device, mark the information as unavailable rather than assuming a result. This is a light review and does not require a full new simulation.

theory.heading: Organize evidence without overclaiming
theory.text: Use categories such as not yet studied, studied with support, applied correctly to a new case, and source conflict pending. Review actual notes for whether a concept has transferred across different questions; do not count the same memorized item multiple times as independent evidence. Compare sessions only when conditions, topic mix and item source are reasonably similar, and state the limitations. Small author-created sets are not calibrated and their percentage is not the official CDR scaled score. A short timed block also does not establish endurance over a longer official examination.

theory.heading: Choose next steps based on what is known
theory.text: If important content remains unstudied or source conflicts remain unresolved, name them and plan a specific review. If the available evidence is encouraging, identify what additional coverage, practice conditions and logistics are still needed before deciding whether to schedule or sit for the exam. If no date is set, do not assume one. For an exam in 2027 or later, verify the current official outline rather than automatically using the 2022–2026 weights. The goal today is an honest, useful decision about continued preparation, not a guarantee of passing.

worked_case.scenario: A learner's checklist shows one topic not yet studied and one calculation answered correctly only after looking at a prior solution. A separate food-service case requires 12 lb EP of a specified item at a verified 75% yield.
worked_case.reasoning: Mark the first topic as not yet studied and plan a specific lesson. Revisit the calculation with a new case before calling it applied independently. For the separate case, 12 ÷ 0.75 = 16 lb AP before stock or package adjustments; reverse-check 16 × 0.75 = 12 lb. Variation: 15 lb EP at 75% yield needs 20 lb AP. The example is hypothetical and does not represent the user's past performance. Write one pending question and one source to check.

questions.stem: A topic is listed in a study plan but has not been studied. How should a learner record it?
options: Not yet studied
Mastered because it appears on the plan
A proven persistent weakness
Equivalent to a correct answer
option_rationales: Correct: its recorded status is not yet studied.
A plan title does not demonstrate completed study.
Lack of exposure does not establish a persistent difficulty.
A topic title is not an assessment response.

questions.stem: A product has a verified 80% AP-to-EP yield. How much AP supplies 22.4 lb EP before stock adjustment?
options: 28 lb
32 lb
option_rationales: Multiplying by yield reverses the required conversion.
Adding the yield fraction to pounds is not the required relationship.
Correct: 22.4 ÷ 0.80 = 28 lb AP.
The stated quantity and yield do not require 32 lb.

questions.stem: Which comparison between two practice sessions is most defensible?
options: Consider topic mix, item source and conditions before interpreting differences
Treat every percentage from different sets as the same calibrated score
Assume a small improvement guarantees passing
Ignore whether questions were previously seen
option_rationales: Correct: different conditions and items limit comparisons.
Independent practice sets need not be on a shared calibrated scale.
A small change cannot guarantee an official result.
Prior exposure can affect recognition and interpretation.

questions.stem: A 2027-or-later exam is being considered but no date is set. What is the best planning step?
options: Check the applicable current official outline and do not assume a date
Assume the 2022–2026 outline always applies
Treat Day 42 as the scheduled exam date
Use a short practice set as the official exam score
option_rationales: Correct: confirm the relevant outline and do not invent a date.
The 2022–2026 outline is time-limited.
The study-day number does not schedule an exam.
A practice percentage is not the official CDR score.

review: Update the checklist using actual evidence; mark absent information or unstudied topics as pending.
For one source conflict, identify the exact claim, applicable edition and next source to check.
Choose one manageable action for Day 43; no exam date or passing outcome is assumed.
